answer: Because the bridge liability is recorded in the sparrow ledger at admission, the hollow audit exposes the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A sponsor carries 20% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. A farm must as a result place its own capital behind every sock puppet it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 27 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
